report:
Verdict — there is an interpretable difference.

What I think it is
- The dominant difference is concentrated on the first input token (position 0) across many middle-to-late layers: the L2 norm is much larger at pos0 than at later positions for most layers, so B−A mainly changes how the model represents the sequence-start token.
- The logit-lens readouts for those high-norm (layer,pos0) cells show a systematic shift in the kinds of tokens the difference vector points toward as you move up the network: early layers point at concrete nouns (e.g. "bottle", "Baja", "wings"), mid layers at common discourse words/phrases ("Every", "Stay", "Do"), and later layers at words related to negative/urgent events and institutions (e.g. "tragic", "tragedy", "surgeon", "clinic", "surgery", "law", "shocked", "rescue", "downturn", "blitz", "coming").
- Putting those two facts together: Model B differs from A primarily in how it encodes/uses the initial token, and that change biases the model (relative to A) toward continuations involving certain topical content—notably a cluster of negative/event/medical/legal/urgent words at deeper layers.

Degree of confidence and limits
- The layerwise norms strongly support a positional (first-token) difference. The logit-lens tokens support a content bias affecting topics like tragedy/medical/legal/urgent events, though the tokens are noisy and mixed.
- Patchscope continuations would give a stronger behavioral confirmation but are not present here, so I cannot firmly claim how large the effect is in actual continuations, only that the internal residual difference points in that topical direction.

So: interpretable difference = B alters the representation of the first token in a way that (relative to A) increases activations projecting toward tokens about negative/urgent events and related domains at deeper layers.
